label: String Ensemble 2, sampled, close and dry
audition_title: libsonare second string ensemble vs the sampled reference
_notes: Every fourth semitone from 48 to 72, two octaves centred where this is written, and the grid the section voices already captured on this rack share. Both ends were rendered before this definition was written and both are healthy.
_velocities: Five, matching the slots of this rack captured earlier so that one axis covers the whole of it. The axis is live here at 26.5 dB between velocity 16 and 104.
_dry: Nothing to switch off, measured rather than assumed: with the rack loaded not one of the plugin's 1526 advertised parameters matches `reverb` or `delay`, so `dry` has no section to act on and is left off rather than claiming an effect was disabled. What the recording contains is answered by `room`, which is a different question.
_room: No room, and the answer has to be declared because no note-tail measurement can reach it: a release and a small hall are the same falling signal over the tail a capture records, and the per-note agreement test that separates a room from one note's decay passes on a release perfectly. `calibrate` measures RT60 0.00 s. With the rack loaded, not one of the 1526 parameters the plugin advertises matches `reverb`, `delay` or `room`, and every slot of it captured in an earlier round recorded no space.
_stimulus: Three seconds, the family's. This voice sustains rather than decaying, so the gate is the length of the measurement rather than a window over an event: it is still sounding 1.6 dB under its peak when the key lifts, which is what makes `damper` measurable here and what the previous reading of this slot said was impossible.
_calibration: From `capture.py calibrate` on this rack, whose settings this capture adopts from the slots of it captured earlier so they stay comparable: a two-second settle against a measured minimum of 250 ms, and two renders of one cell bit-identical, so there is no round robin to put a floor under the loss. `realtime` is kept on although the reference renders the same either way, because a note streamed late is caught only by `verify` and would otherwise be committed as a measurement.
_timbres: One, and the ladder is monotone above it, so this capture cannot move the voice past `voiced` however complete its coverage. That is a property of the source rather than of the work: the rack holds one slot per GM program, so there is no second second string ensemble in it to disagree with, and `source_for` takes every timbre of a capture from one plugin. What the reference does buy is the thing there was none of before -- a measured target for `autofit` and `--diagnose`, in place of voicing this program by ear. A second timbre needs a rack authored with an alternative in it, and this capture is written so that adding one is an edit to this list rather than a re-capture.

timbres.label: GM second string ensemble, rack slot 2

_dimensions: All 10 a sustained voice can be judged on, with none excused. `stereo` is kept and is real here rather than nominal: the two channels differ by +3.4 dB relative to the signal, which is an image rather than the render noise a dual-mono slot shows at -570.
_history: This voice was previously recorded as unusable because its samples were said to stop while the key is still down. Re-measured, they do not: it holds 1.6 dB under its peak at the end of an eight-second gate, and the steepest single 10 ms step anywhere inside the held note is 3.1 dB, which is the instrument's own movement. A sample running out reads quite differently -- the two voices on the neighbouring racks that genuinely do it step 47 and 53 dB in one window and are at the noise floor immediately after.
_identity: Which product this is captured from lives in the untracked sibling `string_ensemble_2.local.json`: the plugin's component triple and the slot's preset. Everything here is the method. Re-capturing needs the overlay; scoring, fitting and diagnosing read `reference/string_ensemble_2.json` and need nothing.
_slots: Slot identity is measured, never taken from a name or a position, and on this rack it is checkable against the repository's own committed measurements: six of its sixteen slots were captured in an earlier round. Rendered under that capture's own gate at a cell its profile holds, slot 9 returns a peak of -13.58 dBFS against a committed -13.58, which fixes slot n as GM program 47+n. Every slot of this rack near this one was compared against its neighbours at both ends of this grid and at its middle, and all are distinct audio -- the sample sharing that three slots of another rack show outside their instruments' ranges does not happen here.
